newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds hold tight range post-tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds hold tight range post-tender.

text.p: Australian bonds held reasonably steady following today's A$700 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender, the first for the 1996/97 fiscal year, traders said.
"The 2008s (bonds) were in demand, but I'm not sure how much of this has already been hedged," one trader added.

By 2.20 p.m. (0420 GMT), the September 10-year bond futures contract had edged down to 91.820 from a pre-tender 91.835. The contract has shed some 30 basis points in the last two sessions in a correction to the sharp rally since June.
The tender offer comprised A$300 million in the Janaury 2001 and A$400 million in the August 2008.
The 2008 stock went off at an average yield of 8.228 percent compared with succesful bids ranging from 8.21 to 8.24 percent
The outstanding stock was trading at around 8.235/8.195 percent at the lunchtime recess.
The 2001 stock, meanwhile, fetched an average yield of 7.634 percent in a bid range of 7.62/7.64 percent. The existing stock had been quoted at around 7.64/7.60 percent when bids went in.
This was the first Treasury bond supply since June 18 and was cited by traders as one of several factors causing the rapid retracement since Friday.

The sell-off, which has taken 10-year bond yields to around 8.20 percent from a post-budget 7.80 percent last week, is largely seen as a corrective move, having descended from over 9.0 percent since mid-June.
A weak U.S. Treasury market, gripped by fears of a tightening in U.S. monetary policy amid a rebounding economy, has also fuelled the trend.
